'''Decipher and the ''Star Wars'' CCG Lucasfilm license''' covers [[Decipher]]'s license to publish SWCCG, its pitch to keep it, and the license's end on 31 December 2001. Lucasfilm then gave the card-game rights to Wizards of the Coast, and Decipher handed SWCCG to the volunteer [[Players Committee]].

== The license ==

Decipher was meeting Lucasfilm at Skywalker Ranch as a licensee by November 1994, while developing its ''Star Wars'' game.<ref name="vapilot1994" /> [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] shipped in December 1995. In 1998 Lucasfilm renewed the license and extended it to ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="wp-swccg" /><ref name="duelist25" />

== The pitch to keep the license ==

[[File:Skywalker-Ranch-presentation-card-encyc.png|thumb|right|300px|The Skywalker Ranch card Decipher showed Lucasfilm.<ref name="encyc3" />]]

In July 2000 Decipher pitched Lucasfilm executives on its plans for the license.<ref name="pres2000" /> It proposed marketing programs (sweepstakes for walk-on roles, set visits and Ranch visits, World Championship prizes, George Lucas signature cards, in-theater promotions, mall tours and fast-food premiums), a digital ''Star Wars'' CCG, and a backward-compatible SWCCG 2nd Edition for 2001. It asked Lucasfilm to treat card games as a core category, give earlier access to film material, ease channel restrictions and avoid over-licensing. Decipher pointed to roughly a quarter of a billion dollars that customers had spent on Decipher's ''Star Wars'' games. Lucasfilm approved none of it.<ref name="pres2000" />

As part of the pitch, Decipher showed Lucasfilm a mock-up Location card, '''•Skywalker Ranch''': "If you occupy, Decipher gets the CCG license here."<ref name="encyc3" />

After the loss, Chairman [[Warren Holland]] said Decipher had offered Lucasfilm more money than for any previous license. He blamed the influence of Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast and a push toward younger, ''Pokémon''-style games. He did not disclose the terms of a settlement with Lucasfilm.<ref name="icv2-2002" /><ref name="tfn2001" />

== End of the license ==

Decipher announced on 28 December 2001 that Lucasfilm would not extend the license.<ref name="ann122801" /><ref name="tfn2001" /> Wizards of the Coast received an exclusive multi-year worldwide trading-card license and planned a new game with ''Episode II'' content for 2002.<ref name="icv2-2002" /> In a special ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' broadcast the same day, Holland said Decipher's manufacturing and sell-off period ran through 30 April 2002.<ref name="rfd-special-0027">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=27s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 00:27. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> He said Decipher's offer to keep the license was more than George Lucas spent to make the original ''Star Wars'' film and six times what Decipher had paid for ''Episode I''.<ref name="rfd-special-0347">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=227s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 03:47. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> The license agreement gave Lucasfilm a contractual right to license Decipher's game mechanics by paying royalties, which it chose not to use, so any new ''Star Wars'' card game would be incompatible with Decipher's.<ref name="rfd-special-1733">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1053s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 17:33. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> Lucasfilm had also turned down the virtual-card design of Decipher's planned last product, ''[[Reflections Gold]]''.<ref name="rfd-special-1923">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1163s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 19:23. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> Decipher could no longer make SWCCG expansions, and cards in development were never released.<ref name="wp-swccg" /> See [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]].

== Handoff to the Players Committee ==

In January 2002 Decipher created the volunteer Players Committee to run tournaments, rulings and support for the game.<ref name="pc1" /> Holland first described the committee in the 28 December 2001 broadcast: a non-profit group of volunteer players and playtesters, given email, web and office support by Decipher, which would take over prize support, the web pages, rules and FAQs and World Championship duties at the end of April 2002, and would post replacement game text for existing cards to make them tournament legal.<ref name="rfd-special-2212">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1332s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 22:12. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> The Committee may issue new cards only electronically and for free, with no new film images; see [[Players Committee-Lucasfilm agreement]] and [[History of the Players Committee]].<ref name="pcabout" />
